newsitem.title: USA: Global offering lifts Mexico Bradies, Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Global offering lifts Mexico Bradies, Eurobonds.

text.p: Taking advantage of the abundant liquidity in the international capital markets, Mexico is racing to offer a $1 billion global bond issue in the new year, analysts and traders said.
The proposed new issue will be fixed-rate, dollar- denominated and mature in 10 years, with Merrill Lynch and Salomon Brothers as joint lead managers.

Mexico has five-year, 20-year and 30-year global bonds outstanding and the 10-year issue would fill the gap on the yield curve, said Tulio Vera, a managing director at Bear Stearns and Co "It is a logical choice."
Inferred from Mexico's quasi-sovereign Eurobond of similar maturity, which trades at 320 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, the new issue is likely to be priced slightly tighter, he said.
The proposed jumbo global issue is timed to cash in on the still ample liquidity in the international capital market, Vera noted.
"The market is receptive to emerging market sovereigns. It should be well received," he added.
With local and congressional elections in Mexico this summer, market jitters could also complicate capital-raising efforts, market sources said.

Recent volatility in the U.S. Treasuries put a dollop of uncertainty in the pricing, but the risk is perceived lower now than in the second half of the year if the U.S. long bond yield continues trending higher, they said.
The economic recovery in Mexico makes the country a strong candidate for credit upgrade, which could happen as early as this spring, one trader said.
"We are upbeat on Mexcio's fundamentals," she said, noting that the market usually prices in the upgrade six to nine months before it actually happens.
Mexcio is rated BB by Standard and Poor's and Ba2 by Moody's Investors service.
Traders said the announcement of the global offering nudged Mexico Bradies higher in a quiet market.

"It focused attention on Mexcio," said a trader, noting the coming roadshows and publicity surrounding the launch would invariably highlight the positive aspects of Mexico's economy and push the prices of existing debt higher.
Mexico UMS-26 MXUMS=RR rose 1-1/2 to 106.00. Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR gained 5/8 to 72-7/8 and Mexico Discount MXFLL19=RR rise 7/8 to 86-7/8.
Elsewhere in the Latin Brady market, Brazil discount Z bond BRFLTD24=RR saw fairly good demand early in the session, which also inspired some sympathy buying in Brazil C BR8D14=RR later on.
Trading in Argentina papers was subdued, with FRBs ARFLC05=RR firmingg 3/8 to 86-3/4 bid.
